summary: Under Armour's pre-2024-05-15 disclosures present a brand-reset story, not a balance-sheet-distress story. The FY23 10-K (PwC, Big-4, 20-year tenure, unqualified ICFR) and Q3FY24 10-Q (Feb-8-2024) show $1.04B cash vs $680.9M total debt, an undrawn $1.1B revolver, and a June-2024 $80.9M convert maturity covered 12.9x. Three historic covenant amendments (2020-2021) are clean fingerprint of past distress that has not reactivated. The negative signals are operational and governance-driven, not solvency-driven: (i) Linnartz's ~14-month CEO tenure ending Mar-31-2024 with founder Plank returning as CEO under super-voting control — a strategic reset that implies the FY23 turnaround plan was abandoned; (ii) Q3FY24 NA revenue -11.8% and wholesale -13.2%, with management self-disclosing PSU performance targets as improbable for both FY23 and FY24 grants; (iii) doubled AR allowance and NA-concentrated goodwill at risk of FY24 impairment review. The 2015-2019 pull-forward securities class action is at the summary-judgment decision point with no accrued reserve. Verdict: NEUTRAL — UA is too liquid and audit-clean to short on framework grounds, but the brand-reset/leadership-instability and demand-deterioration cluster argue against LONG. Composite reflects this: low forensic-lying severity but meaningful Mode-B operational headwinds.
